statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 9 sits well below the block threshold on a US Labor Day session in which no one-way Nasdaq-100 structure has been observed, while Stress 62 reflects a six-week high in crude, elevated Treasury yields and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz escalation.
recommendation: The deterministic Tail-to-action mapping yields EA_ON with Tail 9. A narrow evidence-based danger window is published for 22:00-00:00 UTC, covering the CME Globex equity-futures reopen after the five-hour Labor Day halt, when a thin order book would have to absorb the full holiday information gap. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds a narrow holiday range as the Hormuz tanker war lifts crude to a six-week high
body: US cash equities, the Nasdaq and the SIFMA bond market are closed for Labor Day, and CME equity index futures trade a shortened session that halts at 17:00 UTC before reopening at 22:00 UTC. NQ futures are near 29,600, marginally above Friday's settle in an unusually narrow range; the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Friday at 29,544.15, up 0.21%, roughly 4% below its 30,762 record. The dominant new information is geopolitical: US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers over the weekend after Iranian ballistic-missile fire at US warships, Tehran attacked US-linked vessels in response, and Iran has signalled a restricted maritime zone beyond the Strait of Hormuz in the coming days. Brent is near $97.6 and WTI near $92.5, a six-week high, with crude up roughly 10% over four weeks. Friday's payrolls printed 162K against about 50K expected, pushing the 10-year to about 4.77% and the 2-year to about 4.34% and shifting rate expectations hawkish, yet VIX finished at 15.18, so equity volatility is not yet pricing the energy and geopolitical shock. Breadth is rotational rather than directional: semiconductors were broadly strong on Friday while several megacaps and software names fell, a two-sided tape that historically supports mean reversion. Tail therefore stays low in the absence of observed persistent one-way structure, failed retracements or index extension, while Stress is elevated on the energy, rates and liquidity backdrop. The identified discontinuity mechanisms are the thin futures reopen at 22:00 UTC and Tuesday's 13:30 UTC US cash reopen, which must price two sessions of headlines at once; PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September are the week's scheduled catalysts, with crude at these levels feeding the inflation channel directly.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the last twenty-four hourly Claude assessments were published; the 21:00 UTC slot on 6 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. Across the available hours the mapped state held at EA_ON with Tail between 5 and 8, Stress between 54 and 60 and Confidence between 84 and 86, with a normal dominant mode throughout. The only Tail uptick, to 8 at 22:00 UTC on 6 September, coincided with the weekly futures reopen. The published series therefore shows a quiet, range-bound weekend with no episode of persistent one-way structure or failed retracement.
outlookSummary: The next twenty-four hours are shaped by market structure more than by scheduled data. Tail is expected to sit near current levels through the remaining shortened futures session, fall while CME equity index futures are halted between 17:00 and 22:00 UTC because no price path can form, then rise to its highest published level of the run at the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, when a thin book must absorb the full holiday information gap alongside Iran's pending Hormuz restricted-zone announcement. From there the conditional path normalises through Asian and European hours before a second, smaller step up into the 13:30 UTC US cash reopen on 8 September, the first full-liquidity session since Friday. Every hour maps to EA_ON: this is gap and headline risk, not observed mean-reversion failure. Stress stays elevated throughout on crude near six-week highs, a hawkish rate backdrop after the 162K payrolls print and low outright equity volatility. Confidence eases during the halt, when no live Nasdaq-100 price path is available, and recovers once continuous trading resumes.
